Chromaticism: the force of a semitone
The Tristan chord: a resolution that keeps us waiting
Modes: the white keys change their meaning
Octatonic harmony: eight notes with several centres
Twelve-tone writing: one row, many phrases
Rhythm: two beats can become three
Orchestration: the flute hands over its tune
Spectralism: an ensemble inside a low E
Sonata form presents themes in different keys, develops them, then brings them back in the home key.
An exposition introduces the main themes of a sonata-form movement or the first round of subject entries in a fugue.
The development is the middle section of a sonata-form movement, where earlier themes are altered and taken through other keys.
The recapitulation brings back a sonata-form movement’s opening themes, usually with the later themes now in the home key.
